forces.title: Value Creation Shifts Towards Experience-Driven Property Ecosystems
forces.description: The real estate industry is undergoing a structural shift where value is increasingly created within vibrant, experience-driven ecosystems, combining residential, commercial, and retail elements, rather than standalone assets. This trend, visible in regions like India, emphasizes locations that offer density, interaction, and adaptability, supported by integrated infrastructure and amenities, reshaping performance drivers for mixed-use developments.

forces.title: REIT Market Expansion Provides New Financing Avenues for Retail Assets
forces.description: The rapid growth of India's REIT market, projected to reach US$ 123 billion by 2029 with institutional demand for retail assets, offers significant financing opportunities for retail and mixed-use developers. The RBI's approval for banks to lend to REITs further enhances liquidity and long-term financing, supporting the development and acquisition of income-generating retail real estate assets.

forces.title: Geopolitical Shocks Introduce Cost and Confidence Vulnerabilities
forces.description: Geopolitical conflicts and global disruptions, such as the West Asia conflict, introduce significant risks to the real estate sector, including mixed-use developments. These shocks can lead to elevated energy prices, impacting construction costs, and can transmit through financial market volatility, potentially dampening overall investor and buyer confidence, leading to margin pressures and project delays.

forces.title: ESG Mandates Drive Green Building and Sustainable Development
forces.description: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) considerations are becoming critical for real estate, with assets lacking net-zero plans facing 'brown discounts' and higher financing costs. The growth of green bonds and sustainability-linked loans incentivizes developers to integrate passive design, on-site renewables, and efficient systems. This structural shift towards sustainable development impacts design, construction, and financing for mixed-use projects.

forces.title: AI Integration to Drive Significant Margin Uplift for Mixed-Use Developers
forces.description: AI deployments are expected to deliver a 400-700 basis points margin uplift for real estate development companies, including those focused on mixed-use properties. This stems from AI's ability to optimize revenue growth through better asset monetization and rental optimization, alongside significant cost reductions from improved planning, reduced rework, and predictive maintenance across the development lifecycle.

forces.title: Organized Retail Growth and Global Brand Entry Boost Physical Space Demand
forces.description: The rapid expansion of India's organized retail sector, particularly in Tier-II and Tier-III cities, coupled with the entry of numerous global brands, is driving significant demand for new physical retail spaces. This includes opening of small and medium-format stores, and the development of integrated retail destinations by major players like IKEA and LuLu Group, providing strong tailwinds for retail and mixed-use real estate.

forces.title: Rising Affluence and Luxury Consumption Drive High-End Retail Demand
forces.description: India's expanding high net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth individual populations, coupled with increasing per capita income and strong consumer spending on luxury products, are significant tailwinds for high-end retail and mixed-use developments. This demographic shift fuels demand for premium shopping experiences and lifestyle-oriented spaces, encouraging developers to create sophisticated retail environments.

forces.title: High Upfront Technology Costs and Fragmentation Hinder Digital Adoption
forces.description: Significant upfront capital investment requirements for advanced technology solutions, coupled with a fragmented real estate ecosystem and interoperability issues, pose substantial headwinds to widespread digital adoption. These barriers, including specialized consultancy costs and difficulties in quantifying ROI, particularly challenge smaller and mid-sized developers in the mixed-use segment from achieving scale and efficiency gains.

forces.title: Technology Adoption Becomes Mandatory for Real Estate Capital Access
forces.description: Technology has transitioned from being a competitive differentiator to a fundamental prerequisite for accessing capital and fostering trust in the Indian real estate sector. Developers and operators of mixed-use properties must embed advanced digital capabilities for transparency, rigorous governance, and efficient execution to attract institutional investors and meet evolving market expectations.

forces.title: Favorable FDI Policies and Strategic Partnerships Attract Investment
forces.description: Government policies allowing 100% FDI for townships and settlements, combined with platform-style partnerships between global investors and Indian developers, are significantly boosting investment in mixed-use developments. These initiatives, along with reforms like land digitization, enhance transparency and reduce risks, making the sector more attractive for foreign and domestic capital seeking scalable, long-term real estate strategies.

forces.title: Industrialization of Construction Improves Project Delivery and Quality
forces.description: The adoption of modern construction techniques such as modular construction, robotics, and digital twins is industrializing the real estate development process. This structural change promises enhanced productivity, consistent quality, predictable timelines, and faster speed to market, which is crucial for complex mixed-use projects that require integrated design and efficient execution, unlocking substantial value for developers.

forces.title: Digital Land Registries Enable Fractional Ownership and Asset Tokenization
forces.description: The advancement of digital land registries, supported by initiatives like the National Blockchain Framework, is laying the groundwork for fractional ownership and tokenization of real estate assets. This structural improvement can enhance liquidity, broaden investor participation in mixed-use properties by enabling partial ownership, and create new investment opportunities, especially for assets with transparent and secure digital records.

viewpoints.title: Technology Now a Prerequisite for Real Estate Capital Access and Trust
viewpoints.description: KPMG and FICCI highlight that technology is no longer merely a differentiator but has become a fundamental condition for accessing capital and building trust within the Indian real estate sector. This applies to builders, owners, and operators of commercial and mixed-use environments, emphasizing that transparency, execution intelligence, and rigorous governance frameworks, enabled by technology, are crucial for attracting institutional capital and stakeholder confidence.

viewpoints.title: Organized Retail Expansion Fuels Demand for Physical Store Spaces
viewpoints.description: The Indian organized retail market, currently holding 12% of the total retail market, is projected to expand significantly to 17-19% by 2035. This growth, driven by urbanization, digital adoption, and policy support, is directly fueling demand for physical retail spaces, including shopping malls and high-street retail, as D2C brands and global retailers expand their presence, boosting the retail real estate sector.

viewpoints.title: AI to Deliver Significant Margin Uplift for Mixed-Use Property Developers
viewpoints.description: BCG anticipates AI deployments for real estate development companies (DevCos) focused on mixed-use properties can enable a substantial 400–700 basis points margin uplift. This improvement is expected through enhanced revenue growth and significant cost reduction, driven by efficiencies in planning, construction, and operations. AI's role in optimizing various stages of the development lifecycle presents a strong opportunity for value creation in mixed-use segments.

viewpoints.title: Real Estate Leasing Driving Improved Credit Quality in Services Sector
viewpoints.description: CareEdge Ratings identifies real estate leasing as a key segment contributing to positive credit rating upgrades within the manufacturing and services sectors during H2FY26. This indicates improving financial health and operational performance among companies engaged in real estate leasing, which includes developers and owners of commercial and mixed-use properties, supporting a positive outlook for their credit profiles.

viewpoints.title: Indian Real Estate Shows Structural Strength Amidst Global Headwinds
viewpoints.description: Despite ongoing global disruptions causing cost-side pressures, the Indian real estate sector, including segments like luxury housing (which can be part of mixed-use), maintains structural strength and resilient demand. The report acknowledges potential impacts from geopolitical shocks on construction costs and buyer confidence at the margin, but overall momentum suggests an opportunity, albeit with a need for disciplined execution and prudent financing.

viewpoints.title: REIT Market Growth and Institutional Capital Bolster Retail & Mixed-Use Assets
viewpoints.description: India's Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT) sector has reached a market capitalization of US$ 11.43 billion as of November 2025 and is projected to grow to US$ 123 billion by 2029, driven by institutional demand for office and retail assets. Continued interest in platform-led models, exemplified by investments in entities like Nexus Select Trust, highlights strong investor confidence and financial avenues for retail and mixed-use developments.
